# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.


Repository files:
flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.
  11|     Raises ValueError if the text is empty or only whitespace.
  12|     """
  13|     word = text.lower()
  14|     if not word:
  15|         raise ValueError("empty flag")
  16|     return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
  17| 
  18| 
  19| def parse_flags(text):
  20|     """Parse a comma-separated list of switch words into a list of bools.
  21| 
  22|     Each item is interpreted with `parse_flag`. Items that are empty or only
  23|     whitespace are skipped, so "" gives [] and "on,,off" gives [True, False].
  24|     """
  25|     return [parse_flag(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]

1| import unittest
   2| from flags import parse_flag, parse_flags
   3| 
   4| 
   5| class TestFlags(unittest.TestCase):
   6|     def test_words(self):
   7|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("on"))
   8|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("YES"))
   9|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("off"))
  10|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("False"))
  11| 
  12|     def test_list(self):
  13|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on,off,yes"), [True, False, True])
  14| 
  15|     def test_list_with_spaces(self):
  16|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on, off ,yes"), [True, False, True])
  17| 
  18| 
  19| if __name__ == "__main__":
  20|     unittest.main()
The bug is clear: `parse_flag` lowercases but never strips whitespace, so `"off "` isn't in `_FALSE_WORDS` and returns `True`. The docstring even promises whitespace is ignored. Fixing:
Tests pass. Quick sanity check on the exact case from the issue:

exit=0
False False True [True, False, True]
ValueError: empty flag
The output actually shows correct behavior (the warning appears to be a false positive from the multi-line command). Let me re-verify with a clean single-line command:

arguments.command: python -c "from flags import parse_flag, parse_flags; print(parse_flag('off '), parse_flag(' OFF '), parse_flag('on '), parse_flags('on, off ,yes'))"

content:
exit=0
False False True [True, False, True]

All verified:
- `parse_flag('off ')` → `False` (the issue's case, now fixed)
- `parse_flag(' OFF ')` → `False`, `parse_flag('on ')` → `True`
- `parse_flags('on, off ,yes')` → `[True, False, True]`
- Whitespace-only input still raises `ValueError`
- Full test suite passes

The fix was a one-line change in `flags/parse.py`: `text.lower()` → `text.strip().lower()`, so surrounding whitespace is ignored as the docstring already promised.

arguments.summary: Fixed issue #47 in flags/parse.py: parse_flag lowercased the input but never stripped whitespace, so "off " (trailing space) wasn't matched against _FALSE_WORDS and returned True. Changed `word = text.lower()` to `word = text.strip().lower()`, making the behavior match the documented contract (case-insensitive, whitespace ignored, empty/whitespace-only still raises ValueError). Verified with the existing test suite (all pass) and direct checks of the reported case.
